messages:
olivia: quick report from a customer: Next.js middleware build breaks when importing the main SDK entry. error traces show node:fs and Buffer usage pulled into the edge bundle. they tried runtime='edge' but still saw TS errors about global Request/Response.
ben: that matches our earlier reports. root cause: main entry references node helpers and d.ts references node builtin types.
tara: short-term workaround: import from 'redwood-inference-js/edge' and add `/// <reference lib="webworker"/>` in a local d.ts. but this is rough for new users.
olivia: can we make the UX friction smaller? maybe ship an edge-specific .d.ts automatically and add a clear build-time hint when bundling for edge.
ben: plan: 1) package.json exports map to add ./edge import + types, 2) dist/edge/index.d.ts should include webworker lib triple-slash, 3) add a quickstart snippet and a small eslint rule that warns when the default import is used in files containing `export const runtime = 'edge'`.
tara: i'll draft the exports change and a tiny integration test that builds examples/next-middleware with Next canary. pkg-bot: created branch edge-exports-ux, CI queued.
olivia: thanks—if we can land the docs + types this week it'll close several GH issues. :+1:
